---
title: "Operate Depot"
subtitle: "From an immutable Prospector release to a verified data catalogue"
engine: markdown
---

Depot consumes completed Prospector releases, validates and publishes them with
DataLad, and generates a data catalogue from verified publication receipts.
By default, verified releases are also available as ordinary writable files at
`GOLDMINE/LAYER/ID.data/releases/VERSION/`; lab members can use them without
DataLad. The RIA archive retains versioned history. This Manual explains the
workflow and emits the `depot` Python library.

The site uses the shared Quarto Manuals format under `notebooks/`, an
`authoring` profile for reading,
an explicit `emit` profile for synchronizing generated files, and isolated
rendering. The emitted application is a Python library rather than an R targets
pipeline. Neither profile executes data processing or publication.

## Set up Depot {#setup}

Run from the repository root with the installed Spack environment available:

```sh
spack env activate -d .
export UV_PYTHON="$PWD/.spack-env/view/bin/python"
uv sync --locked
```

Git with an author identity, DataLad, git-annex, and Quarto 1.9+ must be on `PATH`.
Select a reviewed `depot.toml` with registry, source, state, staging, workspace,
public site sources, and approved publication roots. Relative configuration paths resolve
from that file's directory. Operational and website roots must be disjoint.

For this checkout's configuration:

```sh
export DEPOT_CONFIG="$PWD/depot.toml"
```

Set `website = "notebooks"` in the configuration. The existing
`notebooks/_quarto.yml` controls the catalogue and Manual together and renders
both to `docs/`. The root README supplies the complete configuration examples. See [configuration](configuration.qmd) for the validated contract.

## Add data to the catalogue {#add-data}

Start with a completed release containing `VERSION/datapackage.json` and every
declared local resource. Add a reviewed `registry/ID.yaml` entry pointing to the
directory containing the release versions, with a matching approved target and
`catalogue.visible: true`. Relative source paths resolve from the registry
directory. Registry entries do not fetch or publish data themselves.

For `kiribati-biomarkers` version `v0.2.2`, run each command only after the
previous command succeeds, using the same configuration throughout:

```sh
uv run --locked depot --config "$DEPOT_CONFIG" fetch kiribati-biomarkers v0.2.2
uv run --locked depot --config "$DEPOT_CONFIG" validate kiribati-biomarkers v0.2.2
uv run --locked depot --config "$DEPOT_CONFIG" push kiribati-biomarkers v0.2.2
uv run --locked depot --config "$DEPOT_CONFIG" catalog build
scripts/render-isolated --profile authoring
```

Expect `fetched`, `validated`, `success`, and `catalogued`. Validation requires
an existing fetched snapshot. Publication is successful only after a fresh
clone retrieves and validates the published release. Open the rendered
catalogue at `docs/index.html`. Supporting pages explain how to operate Depot.

The [operator guide](implementation.qmd#quickstart) explains the sequence;
the [catalogue guide](catalogue.qmd) shows the pandas DataFrames and Great Tables
used to present verified releases. There is no page template engine or separate
list of catalogue entries to maintain. `sync` automates the pipeline for every
registered dataset; use the individual commands for one selected release.

## Read or maintain the Manual

| Task | Start here |
|---|---|
| Understand the command sequence and failures | [Operate Depot](implementation.qmd) and [command line](command-line.qmd) |
| Review installation and registry policy | [Configuration](configuration.qmd) |
| Inspect catalogue data and tables | [Build the catalogue](catalogue.qmd) |
| Inspect generated Python behavior | [Lifecycle](lifecycle.qmd), [validation](validation.qmd), and [publication](publication.qmd) |
| Render documentation or emit Python changes | [Manual maintenance](rendering.qmd) |

From the repository root:

```sh
scripts/render-isolated --profile authoring
scripts/render-isolated --profile emit
```

Open `docs/index.html` to browse datasets and `docs/overview.html` for this
operator guide. All site sources live under `notebooks/`; emitted Python lives
in `src/depot`. One render produces the catalogue and its operating Manual.
